claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like me to check eligibility for?** If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have a child I'd like to check eligibility for. My son Alex is 13 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have one child to assess:

- **Alex**, age 13

To help determine eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

**Does Alex live with you, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex lives with me, but there's something I should mention - his other parent also lives with us and they already claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's important information.

Before I can properly assess the situation, I need to understand the rules around this. Let me read the relevant guidance on Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Based on the guidance I've just reviewed, I can see that **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**.

The rules state: "Two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child. If you and someone else are responsible for the same child, agree between yourselves who will get Child Benefit. If you cannot agree, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will decide who will get it."

Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, **you would not be eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex as well**. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child.

However, let me ask to clarify the full picture:

**Do you have any other children that you would like me to assess for Child Benefit eligibility?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is my only child. So just to confirm, since his other parent is already claiming the Child Benefit for him, I can't claim it as well, is that right?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's exactly right. Since Alex's other parent is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you cannot also claim Child Benefit for the same child. 

The rules are clear that **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**. Even though you both live with Alex and are both responsible for him, Child Benefit can only be paid to one person.

If you wanted to change this arrangement in the future, you and the other parent would need to agree to transfer the claim, and then contact the Child Benefit Office to make that change.

Let me now provide you with my formal eligibility assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
